issue.title: Custom agents: use current runtime settings in SDK runner turns
issue.acceptance:
A saved agent can change its runtime or SDK runner without changing its identity (#11966), but the host passes its pinned definition to the SDK runner after choosing its latest runtime/model. Changing runner A to B therefore fails before the child starts. Changing a native runtime to SDK also sends a non-SDK agent definition.

Source evidence (current main):
- `apps/openagents/crates/engine/src/doc_host/custom_agents.rs:181-194` selects current same-identity settings and resolves the runtime/model.
- `custom_agents.rs:226-231` serializes `a.definition.spec`, the old pinned definition, into `openagentsAgentSpec`.
- `apps/openagents/crates/harness/src/sdk.rs:165-172` rejects a runner definition whose model differs from the run request; the shared runner Turn also validates the SDK definition.

Bounded fix: pass the selected current settings to the existing SDK runner input. Keep assignment identity, permissions, installed executable registration, cancellation, and native execution paths intact. No runtime migration or provider/auth changes.

Acceptance:
- Updating the runner on the same agent supplies matching runtime/model and pinned instructions/access to the ordinary SDK runner turn.
- Changing a native agent to SDK supplies an SDK definition.
- Identity edits still use the pinned revision, and existing bindings/cancellation tests pass.

Dependencies: built on shipped #11903, #11906, #11908, #11916, and #11966; no open dependency. …

state.last_comment: Implementation is committed locally as 6e6e0e7bd1 on codex/custom-runtime-parity. It binds the current same-identity settings and resolved SDK runtime/model into the existing runner request; regression cases cover SDK runner changes and native-to-SDK changes while preserving assignment revision, instructions, and access. rustfmt and git diff --check pass. Targeted engine custom_agents tests have not executed: the coordinator requested stopping the build at the 30 GiB disk floor, and Cargo exited 130 before the engine test binary linked. No deployment, app restart, owner-account test, …

why: At 19:58 CDT nothing naming #12018 was on main: the fix existed only as local commit 6e6e0e7bd1 on codex/custom-runtime-parity, never pushed.

issue.title: Expose cached Codex account quota through OpenAgents CLI with explicit freshness
issue.acceptance:
## Acceptance criteria

- Resolve host and account deterministically, with explicit missing/ambiguous selection errors. Querying never activates or switches an account.
- Default to reading the existing shared engine cache. Do not introduce another provider polling path or persistent cache.
- Provide stable machine-readable output with selected host/account, plan, all supplied quota windows and reset timestamps, fetched timestamp, observation time/age, and documented fresh/stale/never-fetched/unavailable state. Include errors independently of last-good cached windows.

- Document CLI examples, JSON field/time semantics, refresh behavior, and exit behavior for unavailable/stale/error cases. Avoid printing credentials or credential-related transport internals. …

issue.title: Partition OpenCode model catalogs by the OpenAgents inference credential
issue.acceptance:
OpenCode model catalogs do not change partitions when the OpenAgents inference credential changes.

Source evidence:
- `crates/openagents-web/src/cloud_host.rs:87` configures OpenCode with `{env:OPENAGENTS_API_KEY}`; lines 546–550 pass the account credential to the cloud engine.
- `apps/openagents/crates/harness/src/model_context.rs:127` fingerprints OpenCode environment variables only with the prefixes `OPENCODE_`, `OPENAI_`, `ANTHROPIC_`, and `GOOGLE_`. It omits `OPENAGENTS_API_KEY`.
- `apps/openagents/crates/engine/src/model_catalogs.rs:24` selects the disk catalog by this context hash, and line 77 checks that the context has not changed before accepting a live result. The harness also keys its in-memory catalog by this context.

A changed or revoked OpenAgents key can therefore leave discovery in the old credential partition. This is a confirmed model-discovery contract defect, not a claimed cause of the missing iOS controls/streaming reported in #12020.

Acceptance:
- Changing or removing `OPENAGENTS_API_KEY` changes the OpenCode model context fingerprint; no credential bytes appear in the result.
- Existing provider environment matching remains intact and unrelated harnesses do not acquire the OpenAgents inference key as a dependency.
- Cover the actual environment-selection/hash path with deterministic fixtures, without changing process credentials or touching an account. …

landed.subject: Include the OpenAgents key in OpenCode catalog partitions (#12021)

state.last_comment:
Done in d89d268a57 on main (builds on the d5684f2a13 checkpoint).

- OpenCode's model context fingerprint now hashes `OPENAGENTS_API_KEY`. Changing or removing the key moves discovery to a new catalog partition, and the result is a SHA-256 hex digest, so no key bytes appear in it. Existing OpenCode provider prefixes still match, and Claude Code, Codex and Pi don't hash the key.
- Two deterministic fixture tests drive the real environment-selection/hash path. No process environment or account is touched. …

why: d89d268a57 adds OPENAGENTS_API_KEY to the OpenCode context fingerprint with fixture tests; the one failing harness test also fails on plain main and is tracked in #12024.

issue.title: Show execution-host Codex account usage on the iOS Talk with Codex screen
issue.acceptance:
## Acceptance criteria

- Display the relevant host and active Codex account/plan, available quota windows and percentages, and reset times when supplied by the existing data source.
- While a call is active, bind usage to that call's actual host/account. While idle, use the chosen/default host for the next call. Do not relabel an active call using changed next-call preferences.
- Load usage without requiring a paid voice call to start. Refresh using the existing account-usage caching, throttling, and retry/backoff conventions.
- Handle loading, no host, offline, sign-in required, unsupported/unavailable, and stale/error states honestly. Preserve fetch timestamps; missing data must not appear as zero usage or an invented balance.
- The display must not switch accounts, restart calls, or change voice preferences. Keep transport and state ownership in Rust with Swift presentation.
- Validate host/account selection, host changes and late replies, and missing/failed/stale usage data with focused tests. Include UI validation where feasible without disrupting a running call.

issue.title: iOS: show Working while a saved account chat answers
issue.acceptance:
A confirmed account-chat presentation bug: the saved account transcript on iOS never shows its existing Working indicator while an answer is running. This is separate from the reported new session on a selected cloud computer; it is not established as the cause of that report.

Acceptance:
- Sending in a saved account chat shows Working before text arrives and while the answer is in progress, using the existing transcript indicator.
- Completion, stop, failure, paused observation, account switch, and chat switch do not leave a Working row.
- Streaming content, tool rows, cancellation, retry identity, and local computer sessions retain their current behavior.
- Focused adapter/layout regressions pass; no production account test or app restart.

Ownership: `apps/openagents/crates/mobile/src/client_ffi/saved.rs`, focused tests in the same file and `layout/tests.rs` only if needed; one integration note in `apps/openagents/docs/downstream-patches.md`. No generated FFI, voice, client account wrappers, engine, SDK, or custom-agent files.

Dependencies: uses closed #11893 send/stream/stop and the current Turns snapshot. No backend dependency. Desktop and the first-screen account chat are assessed and reported separately; this issue is bounded to saved-account iOS Working presentation.

landed.subject: Show Working while a saved account chat answers on iOS (#12019)
Add the #12019 on-device check to After-close checks

issue.title: Build caches grow without bound: host-level sweep to keep 100 GiB free without any agent session
issue.acceptance:
Seen 2026-10-17: free disk on the owner's Mac fell from 262 GiB at 2:06 PM to 32 GiB at 6:25 PM CDT with no one watching. `~/work/openagents-target-1-app` grew from empty to 328 GiB and `openagents-target-1` to 208 GiB in about 4 hours. Every worktree path recompiles the workspace crates and feature variants into the same shared target, and nothing ever evicts old artifacts. A new per-agent copy (`openagents-target-agent2-app`, 34 GiB) also appeared despite #11971. Earlier today the same thing happened at 33 GiB and again at 95 GiB.

Foreman's watch only alerts while its own session is alive, so cleanup can't depend on it.

## Fix
- A host-level sweep that runs without any agent session (the build gate from #11971 in `coder-lease`, or a launchd/engine timer), keeping the owner's floor of **100 GiB free**:
  - LRU eviction inside shared targets: delete `debug/deps`, `debug/build` and `incremental` entries not used for N hours when a target exceeds a size cap (default 120 GiB per target).
  - Delete whole shared targets that no running cargo, rustc or kache process holds (check each process's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and cwd) when the disk is under the floor. …

Done when the code is on main with tests (a fake target tree plus fake processes covering eviction, in-use protection and floor behavior) and the sweep is installed on this Mac. Live check: the disk stays above 100 GiB through a day of agent builds.

landed.subject: Add a build sweep that keeps 100 GiB free with no agent session

state.last_comment: Fixed in 58559c745b (main). `coder_lease::agent_builds::sweep`, beside the #11971 build gate, runs from launchd every 5 minutes as `~/.openagents/bin/openagents-build-sweep` (`com.openagents.build-sweep`, installed on this Mac 2026-10-17 6:51 PM CDT). why: 58559c745b adds the coder-lease sweep with fake-tree tests and the launchd job, and the #12023 chat installed it on the Mac; the day-long live check doesn't hold the issue.
